1500.title: The Land That Fed the Wars
1500.description: Most people were farmers. Rice sustained the economy, paid taxes to the daimyō, and ultimately financed the armies fighting across Japan.

1500.title: War Builds a City
1500.description: As daimyō strengthened their domains, castle towns grew around their fortresses, drawing farmers, artisans and merchants into a new urban economy.

1500.title: The Lower Rise
1500.description: Sengoku society was unusually fluid. Through military skill and political opportunity, men of humble origins could rise far beyond the status of their birth.

1500.title: The Gunpowder Revolution
1500.description: After Portuguese matchlocks arrived in 1543, Japanese armies adopted firearms rapidly, transforming battlefield tactics and even the armor worn by warriors.

1500.title: A New Place in the World
1500.description: In an age of gekokujō, birth did not always determine destiny. Military achievement could carry a man from the fields into the service of powerful lords.
